A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same I2VControl work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references. Inspection through their final pages establishes that neither supplied PDF includes an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments, including trajectory-control and motion-brush measurements in Tables 2–3 and qualitative results in Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and reports additional camera-control results and user-study scores in Tables 2–4.

M1.justification: The motion-unit partitioning, rigid-plus-residual representation, control tensor, adapter integration, and inference procedure are retained. v3 adds implementation explanations and applications to other backbones, without specifying a revised control algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds dedicated camera-control evaluation on RealEstate10K and MO, covering static-scene camera movement and scenes with camera and other motion. VIPSeg and the manually constructed dragging, object-brush, and fluid-brush coverage are retained; their revised names do not establish new datasets.

E2.justification: MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl become experimentally evaluated comparators in v3's camera-control comparisons (Table 3 and Figure 9); v1 only included them in discussion and the feature-comprehensiveness table. DragAnything, MOFA-Video, and Motion-I2V remain in their corresponding empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 introduces camera evaluation using RotErr and TransErr, trains MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl on the same base model and data as I2VControl, and adds a User score across the comparisons. It also reports training on Seedance and Wan 2.1. The User score's scale, participants, and procedure are unspecified. These additions do not establish reruns of the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v3 Section 5.3.3 adds a limited portability analysis on Seedance and Wan 2.1, reporting that the framework works with both. The PDF provides only a qualitative assertion and external links for further evidence. Neither version reports component ablations or sensitivity studies, and the earlier capability demonstrations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added User scores are point values without a disclosed uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing ObjMC, FID, MSC, and IoU values remain unchanged in the matched comparisons. v3 adds camera-control results, user scores, and camera examples. For example, Table 3 reports RealEstate10K RotErr of 0.52 for I2VControl, versus 2.69 for MotionCtrl and 1.19 for CameraCtrl. These are newly reported comparisons, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.2 explicitly states rigid-transformation invariance of motion strength in Equation 7; v3 omits this formal property. The principal trajectory, partition, rigid-fitting, and motion-strength definitions remain equivalent despite reorganization and renumbering.

C1.justification: v3's introduction adds an explicit priority claim that I2VControl is the first framework combining camera control, object dragging, and motion brush without conflicts. The underlying claims of unified control, flexible combinations, architecture independence, and strong performance were already present in v1.

C2.justification: v3 adds concrete explanations of conflicts between camera control and dragging or brushing, plus a perception-generation dual-task rationale for constructing training data. Section 5.3.2 newly discusses inconsistent baseline setups and unavailable unified-control comparisons, while asserting that remaining performance differences arise from methods rather than base models. The earlier motion-brush interpretation remains.

D1.justification: Reproducibility documentation changes substantially: v3 names SpatialTracker, specifies MSE-only training, supplies adapter pseudocode and tensor shapes, and states that Wan 2.1 code has been released. Conversely, it omits v1's 16-A100 configuration, batch size, 100K-step training description, explicit test-set counts, and dense-trajectory ObjMC qualification. These omissions do not establish actual setting changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Peekaboo, SpatialTracker, Seedance, Wan, and the work associated with RealEstate10K, while removing StreamingT2V, CamCo, and NUWA-XL. It also makes the priority claim explicit. Most prior-work relationships remain intact, so this is a limited positioning update.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, related work is condensed, and a new Preliminary and Rethinking section separates conceptual motivation and trajectory definitions from the method. Training-data construction and inference are regrouped as a dual task pair, and the experimental narrative is reorganized.

P2.justification: v3 expands Figure 1 with a combined-control example and adds diagrams for control conflicts, dual tasks, motion-unit extraction, and adapter computation, plus a camera-comparison figure. Existing figures are resized or relocated. Tables gain User rows, a new camera-results table is introduced, and the brush-results table is substantially restructured.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens a central capability's validation through dedicated camera-control comparisons on two datasets with matched base models and training data, and its diagrams and reorganized explanation improve accessibility. The net gain is limited by unexplained User scores, removal of important training and sample-count details, and backbone-portability evidence that is largely external to the PDF.
